plainTranslation: A's identity meets B's dreams. The opposition pulls them into push-and-pull.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.

summaryDeep: Their sense of identity, confidence, and direction press against your imagination, hope, and idealism. It catches often enough that you both feel it, and it keeps asking to be worked out. Name it directly instead of letting it build in silence.
tension: Oppositions invite projection. Each person can start relating to an image instead of the person. The Sun person may become the answer, while the Neptune person becomes the dream. Over time, it gets harder to tell what is real and what is imagined. This connection is healthiest when both people allow the illusion to fall away and get to know each other as they truly are. The attraction often grows in the space between what is known and what is imagined. Each person may begin filling in the missing pieces with hopes, assumptions, or longings of their own. When reality eventually challenges those expectations, the letdown can feel surprisingly intense. Neither person may have intended to create an illusion, yet both can end up feeling confused by the difference between what they believed and what was actually there.
advice: The invitation here is to keep returning to the person in front of you. Ask yourself what is actually true. Notice where you are filling in the blanks. Disappointment is not always a sign that something has gone wrong. Sometimes it is simply the moment when reality arrives and asks to be included. This connection can be deeply beautiful when both people allow room for mystery without abandoning truth.
summaryShort: Their sense of identity, confidence, and direction press against your imagination, hope, and idealism.
